s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive ocular and musculoskeletal abnormalities with onset in adolescence
salient_findings: Hypermobility of shoulders, digits, and knees
key_facts: Age of onset of elevated intraocular pressure: 13 years
Patient's height: 180.4 cm
Presence of long fingers
Hypermobility of shoulders, digits, and knees
Family history of similar findings: negative
Serial echocardiograms: no abnormalities
Open iridocorneal angle in each eye
No evidence of Haab striae, buphthalmos, or high iris insertion
Subtle lens dislocation superonasally in the right eye first observed at age 17
Lens dislocation in the left eye developed at age 32
Genetic testing revealed 2 heterozygous variants in the LTBP2 gene

shortlist.label: Weill-Marchesani syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by ectopia lentis, short stature is not a requirement and some patients have tall stature, and it can present with glaucoma

shortlist.label: Marfan syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Features include tall stature, ectopia lentis, and joint hypermobility, which align with the patient's presentation

shortlist.label: Homocystinuria
shortlist.why_kept: Causes ectopia lentis, glaucoma, and can have tall stature, but the absence of intellectual disability and thromboembolic events makes it less likely

shortlist.label: LTBP2-related ocular syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: The patient has genetic variants in the LTBP2 gene, which is associated with this syndrome characterized by glaucoma and ectopia lentis

shortlist.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Features joint hypermobility and can have ocular manifestations, but the specific combination of findings in this patient is less typical for this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of two heterozygous variants in the LTBP2 gene, along with the clinical findings of elevated intraocular pressure, lens dislocation, and open iridocorneal angle, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Weill-Marchesani syndrome
rejected.why: Typically associated with short stature, brachydactyly, and joint stiffness, which are not present in this patient.

rejected.label: Marfan syndrome
rejected.why: Usually involves significant cardiovascular and skeletal abnormalities, which are not evident in this case.

rejected.label: Homocystinuria
rejected.why: Typically presents with intellectual disability, thromboembolism, and other systemic features not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
rejected.why: While hypermobility is a feature, the specific ocular findings and genetic results in this case are more consistent with LTBP2-related ocular syndrome.

gold: Juvenile-onset glaucoma with compound heterozygous LTBP2 mutations
